question: Does independently measured background displacement explain first assignment loss232 at539?
hypothesis: Abrupt background displacement shifts observed boxes outside the uncompensated prediction; fixed background correction can remove the local rejection.
method: Sequential decode, no neural model. Track Shi-Tomasi points using pyramidal Lucas-Kanade with forward/backward consistency. Exclude detector boxes conf>=0.1 expanded20px on both ends, and fixed target exclusion900,475,1100,620. Fit a similarity transform on even 80px grid cells with RANSAC; assess held-out odd cells. Fit both537->538 and538->539 before inspecting assignments. Primary full transform; residual H538_539 @ inverse(H537_538) checks double-counting existing camera drift. Evaluate target-row-only and all-row geometric corrections on the frozen full539 matrix; preserve original score correction differences. Reverse transform is a direction control. No trajectory replay.
acceptance: All original input hashes and saved539 cost matrix/assignment reproduce before intervention.
Both background transforms have at least50 train and50 heldout points, heldout median error<=2px and90th percentile<=5px; target excluded. Failed readiness remains inconclusive, no parameter search.
At unchanged cost limit0.8 report the exact selected raw detection and all competitor changes for every registered arm; no full-tracker or true-identity gain inferred.
limits: Background transform is an image-motion estimate, not external camera pose. Dynamic unmasked objects, parallax and depth may remain. No direct GT annotation at539; even restored assignment cannot prove true identity. Camera correction is an isolated counterfactual, not unique physical cause. Literature BoT-SORT https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.14651 supports mechanism only.
